name: Drakeyard Pigment Crop Tank
description:
A cropped tank top in a garment-dyed cotton-analog that takes pigment in deep, slightly uneven washes — each batch comes out a little different, which is the point. Cut with a wide, low armhole and a straight hem that sits two inches above the waist. Neckline is a generous scoop. The fabric is lightweight but not sheer, with enough body to drape rather than cling. Common colors: acid-washed indigo, rust-dye terracotta, a particular muddy sage, and a near-black that fades to charcoal after washing.

Drakeyard is a street-level brand operating out of a dye workshop in the Tier 2/3 border corridor. The tanks are sold at popup markets, through a small network of independent boutiques, and via word of mouth. They have an outsized cultural footprint for their size — worn by musicians, athletes, and people who just want something that looks good without trying to look expensive. The crop is wearable on most bodies; the wide armhole accommodates augmented shoulder profiles naturally.
what_it_says: You know where to look. You're not buying into anything manufactured — you're buying into something made.
story_hooks: A specific dye batch from Drakeyard has been producing an unexpected bioluminescent afterglow in UV light — the dye source is unregistered and possibly geneware-derived.
The Drakeyard workshop is being pressured to relocate by a Tier 4 corridor development project; the owner is considering more direct forms of resistance.
A character tracking a missing person follows a trail of Drakeyard tanks — three people, all wearing the same rust-dye batch, all disappeared within a week of each other.
